[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

A Golden Path defines what a system should look like, but without a machine-executable specification of what "conforming to this path" means, conformance is an informal assertion. There is no way to automatically verify that a developer or AI agent has actually built within the path's constraints — compliance claims cannot be substantiated.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

A Verification Contract is the machine-readable specification that accompanies every Golden Path and defines — for each structural rule of the path — the automated check that verifies compliance. It is the integration point between the human-readable path definition and the automated verification infrastructure (conformance gates, fitness functions, policy-as-code, runtime monitors). A Golden Path without a Verification Contract is not publishable.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- During authorship of every new Golden Path (concurrent, not after)
- When updating a Golden Path with new structural rules
- When onboarding a new verification tool that must integrate with existing contracts
- When defining the acceptance criteria for an AI-generated output
page_texts.7:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#target-audience]

### Target Audience

This pattern is intended for:

- **Enterprise Architects** defining governance frameworks and standards
- **Platform Engineers** implementing and operating governed platform capabilities
- **Solutions Architects** applying governance patterns in solution design
- **DevOps Engineers** integrating governance controls into delivery pipelines
page_texts.8:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- **Conformance is verifiable, not asserted**: "This system conforms to GP-001" is backed by a passing automated verification suite, not a human claim.
- **Compliance evidence by construction**: Every build run against the Verification Contract generates structured, timestamped compliance evidence.
- **AI agent quality gate**: AI-generated output that passes the Verification Contract is as trustworthy as human-authored output that passes the same contract.
- **Path evolution is safe**: When a path changes, the Verification Contract changes with it, and adopters can detect whether their implementation still conforms.
page_texts.10:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

The [Enterprise Architecture Verification Strategy](../../../strategy/white-papers/engineering/enterprise-architecture-verification-strategy.md) establishes that verification is a design requirement of every Golden Path, not a post-build addition. The Verification Contract is the specific artifact that operationalizes this requirement. It is the document that makes "verification by construction" concrete rather than aspirational.

Without a Verification Contract, a Golden Path review by the ARB is evaluating narrative documentation — it cannot verify that the claimed configuration is actually enforced in the template. With a Verification Contract, the ARB can evaluate both the path specification and its machine-executable compliance proof.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

The Verification Contract is a machine-readable YAML document that maps each structural rule of a Golden Path to an automated check. The automated checks are implemented by the four verification layers: conformance gates (PTN-INFRA-GOV-001), fitness functions (PTN-APP-GOV-001), policy-as-code (PTN-INFRA-GOV-002), and runtime monitors (PTN-APP-GOV-003). The Verification Contract is written alongside the path and reviewed as part of the same ARB gate.
page_texts.12:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

Without a Verification Contract:
- A path specifies "all services must expose a `/health` endpoint" but there is no check — teams miss it and AI agents generate paths without it.
- A path specifies "no PHI in application logs" but there is no automated verification — the rule exists only in documentation and is not enforced.
- When a path is updated (e.g., a new secret management requirement is added), there is no way for existing implementations to know whether they still conform.
- Compliance auditors ask for evidence of path conformance; the only available evidence is "we told teams to follow the path."
page_texts.13:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- The Verification Contract must be authored by the same team that authors the path and reviewed in the same ARB review cycle — it is not a separate deliverable.
- The contract must reference real, executable automation — not aspirational checks.
- The contract must cover all eight verification types defined in the Enterprise Architecture Verification Strategy, or explicitly document why a type is not applicable for this path class.
page_texts.15:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

The Verification Contract Pattern defines the structure, content requirements, and authorship process for the machine-readable compliance specification that accompanies every Golden Path in the catalog. Each contract covers eight mandatory verification types and maps each to a specific automated check at a specific verification layer.

### Architecture Diagram

```
[Verification Contract — Integration Points]

Golden Path Definition (human-readable)
          │

Verification Contract (YAML) ─────────────────────────────┐
          │                                                │
          │ consumed by                                    │ stored in
          ▼                                                ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐   Compliance Evidence Store
│  Four Verification Layers                   │   (PTN-GOV-AI-004)
│                                             │
│  Layer 1: Conformance Gates (build time)    │
│  └─ Checks: structural, dependency, metadata│
│                                             │
│  Layer 2: Fitness Functions (pipeline)      │

│                                             │
│  Layer 3: Policy-as-Code (pre-deploy)       │
│  └─ Checks: infrastructure, network policy  │
│                                             │

│  └─ Checks: behavioral invariants, drift    │
```

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| Verification Contract YAML | Machine-readable specification of all checks for a Golden Path | Golden Path definition |
| Conformance Gate Checks (Layer 1) | Structural and metadata checks at build time | PTN-INFRA-GOV-001 |
| Fitness Function Checks (Layer 2) | Architectural rule checks during CI/CD pipeline | PTN-APP-GOV-001 |
| Policy-as-Code Checks (Layer 3) | Infrastructure compliance checks pre-deployment | PTN-INFRA-GOV-002 |
| Runtime Monitor Checks (Layer 4) | Behavioral and drift checks post-deployment | PTN-APP-GOV-003 |
| Compliance Evidence Store | Stores pass/fail evidence from all checks | PTN-GOV-AI-004 |
page_texts.18:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

1. A Golden Path author creates the path definition. Simultaneously, they author the Verification Contract, specifying for each of the eight verification types: the rule being enforced, the layer (1–4) enforcing it, the specific tool/check implementing it, and the expected pass condition.
2. The Verification Contract is included in the Golden Path ARB submission. The ARB review covers both the path specification and the Verification Contract — if either is incomplete, the path is not approved.
3. When a system is built from the Golden Path (by a developer or AI agent), each applicable check in the Verification Contract is executed by the corresponding verification layer. Pass/fail results are written to the Compliance Evidence Store (PTN-GOV-AI-004) with timestamp, build ID, and path version reference.
4. The Compliance Evidence Store can be queried to produce a conformance report for any system: "Does this system pass all checks in its declared Golden Path's Verification Contract?"
page_texts.19:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

- **Minimal contract** (for experimental paths): A subset contract covering only Layer 1 (conformance gates) is permitted for `experimental`-status paths. Promotion to `active` requires the full eight-type contract.
- **Inherited contract sections**: A path that extends another path (e.g., "FedRAMP REST Microservice" extends "HIPAA REST Microservice") can inherit contract sections from the parent path and add delta checks.

### Prerequisites

- Golden Path Catalog governance model in place (PTN-GOV-AI-001)
- All four verification layers provisioned (PTN-INFRA-GOV-001, PTN-APP-GOV-001, PTN-INFRA-GOV-002, PTN-APP-GOV-003)

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#phase-1-define-the-contract-schema-month-1]

#### Phase 1: Define the Contract Schema (Month 1)

1. Publish the Verification Contract YAML schema (see configuration example below) to the EA Reference Architecture repository as a versioned standard.
2. Add Verification Contract review to the ARB Golden Path review checklist — a path missing a complete contract cannot be approved.
3. Create a Verification Contract authorship guide as part of the Platform Engineering team's onboarding documentation.
page_texts.24:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#phase-2-author-contracts-for-initial-catalog-months-16]

#### Phase 2: Author Contracts for Initial Catalog (Months 1–6)

1. For each of the initial 5–7 Golden Paths, author a complete Verification Contract concurrent with the path definition.
2. Implement the specific checks referenced in each contract in the appropriate verification layer (conformance gate scripts, fitness function tests, OPA/Rego policies, runtime alert rules).
3. Validate each contract by running the full verification suite against a known-good implementation of the path. All checks must pass.
page_texts.25:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#phase-3-maintain-contracts-over-time-month-7]

#### Phase 3: Maintain Contracts Over Time (Month 7+)

1. When a Golden Path is updated (any version bump), update the Verification Contract concurrent with the path change. A breaking path change (MAJOR version) requires updating all affected checks.
2. Track contract coverage: which of the eight verification types are covered for each path. Report uncovered types as technical debt items with remediation timelines.
page_texts.26:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#verification-layer-selection-guide]

### Verification Layer Selection Guide

When authoring a new Verification Contract check, use this guide to assign it to the correct layer:

| Check Property | Recommended Layer | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| File/directory presence or absence | Layer 1 (Conformance Gate) | Pure structural — no execution needed |
| Dependency version or registry validation | Layer 1 (Conformance Gate) | Evaluable from manifest file |
| Compliance annotations in manifests | Layer 1 (Conformance Gate) | Static metadata check |
| PHI in log output | Layer 2 (Fitness Function) | Requires running service to capture logs |
| Endpoint presence and response contract | Layer 2 (Fitness Function) | Requires service invocation |
| Secrets not in environment variables | Layer 2 (Fitness Function) | Requires inspecting runtime configuration |
| Infrastructure encryption at rest | Layer 3 (Policy-as-Code) | Evaluated against Terraform plan before provisioning |
| IAM/RBAC policy compliance | Layer 3 (Policy-as-Code) | Evaluated against plan or manifest |
| Network policy egress/ingress rules | Layer 3 (Policy-as-Code) | Evaluated against Kubernetes manifest |
| Audit events emitted during normal operation | Layer 4 (Runtime Monitor) | Only verifiable post-deployment at scale |
| Configuration drift (manual patches) | Layer 4 (Runtime Monitor) | Detected by comparing live state to declared state |
| Business rule invariants under load | Layer 4 (Runtime Monitor) | Only observable in production traffic patterns |

**General rule**: Assign a check to the earliest layer that can reliably detect the violation. Earlier detection is always cheaper to remediate.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#example-1-verification-contract--hipaa-rest-microservice-gp-001]

#### Example 1: Verification Contract — HIPAA REST Microservice (GP-001)

```yaml
# catalog/verification-contracts/GP-001-verification-contract.yaml
contract_id: 'VC-GP-001'
golden_path_id: 'GP-001'
golden_path_version: '1.2.0'
contract_version: '1.2.0'
status: 'active'

verifications:
  structural_conformance:
    layer: 1
    description: 'Repository structure matches GP-001 scaffold'
    tool: 'conformance-gate-scripts'
    checks:
      - id: 'SC-001'
        rule: 'src/ directory present with required subdirectories (api/, domain/, infrastructure/)'
        command: 'conformance-check --path-id GP-001 --check structural'
        expected: pass
      - id: 'SC-002'
        rule: 'openapi.yaml present at /docs/openapi.yaml'
        command: 'conformance-check --path-id GP-001 --check openapi-spec'
        expected: pass
      - id: 'SC-003'
        rule: 'health endpoint defined in OpenAPI spec'
        command: 'conformance-check --path-id GP-001 --check health-endpoint'
        expected: pass

  dependency_rules:
    layer: 1
    description: 'Dependencies conform to approved library versions'
    tool: 'dependency-validator'
    checks:
      - id: 'DEP-001'
        rule: 'No prohibited dependencies (see dependency deny-list v2.3)'
        command: 'dep-check --deny-list v2.3'
        expected: pass
      - id: 'DEP-002'
        rule: 'All dependencies from approved registries only'
        command: 'dep-check --registry-allow-list'
        expected: pass

  secret_handling:
    layer: 2
    description: 'No secrets in environment variables; approved secret store integration'
    tool: 'fitness-function-runner'
    checks:
      - id: 'SEC-001'
        rule: 'No secrets in environment variables (checked via ESO configuration)'
        fitness_function: 'ff-hipaa-rest/secret-handling'
        expected: pass
      - id: 'SEC-002'
        rule: 'External Secrets Operator referenced in deployment manifest'
        fitness_function: 'ff-hipaa-rest/eso-integration'
        expected: pass

  observability:
    layer: 2
    description: 'Standard observability instrumentation present'
    tool: 'fitness-function-runner'
    checks:
      - id: 'OBS-001'
        rule: 'Prometheus metrics endpoint exposed on /metrics'
        fitness_function: 'ff-hipaa-rest/metrics-endpoint'
        expected: pass
      - id: 'OBS-002'
        rule: 'Structured JSON logging configured (no PHI in log fields)'
        fitness_function: 'ff-hipaa-rest/structured-logging'
        expected: pass

  infrastructure_policy:
    layer: 3
    description: 'Terraform plan conforms to GP-001 infrastructure policy'
    tool: 'opa-rego'
    checks:
      - id: 'INF-001'
        rule: 'Encryption at rest enabled on all storage resources'
        policy: 'policies/golden-paths/gp-001/encryption-at-rest.rego'
        expected: pass
      - id: 'INF-002'
        rule: 'Network policy present restricting egress to approved destinations'
        policy: 'policies/golden-paths/gp-001/network-policy.rego'
        expected: pass

  compliance_metadata:
    layer: 1
    description: 'HIPAA compliance annotations present and correct'
    tool: 'conformance-gate-scripts'
    checks:
      - id: 'META-001'
        rule: 'HIPAA scope annotation present in deployment manifest'
        command: 'conformance-check --path-id GP-001 --check hipaa-annotation'
        expected: pass
      - id: 'META-002'
        rule: 'Golden Path ID and version declared in deployment manifest'
        command: 'conformance-check --path-id GP-001 --check path-declaration'
        expected: pass

  network_policy:
    layer: 3
    description: 'Kubernetes NetworkPolicy conforms to GP-001 specification'
    tool: 'opa-rego'
    checks:
      - id: 'NET-001'
        rule: 'Ingress restricted to API Gateway only'
        policy: 'policies/golden-paths/gp-001/ingress-restriction.rego'
        expected: pass

  runtime_invariants:
    layer: 4
    description: 'Service exhibits required runtime behaviors post-deployment'
    tool: 'deployment-smoke-tests'
    checks:
      - id: 'RT-001'
        rule: 'Health endpoint returns 200 within 60 seconds of deployment'
        test: 'smoke-tests/gp-001/health-check.test'
        expected: pass
      - id: 'RT-002'
        rule: 'Metrics endpoint reachable by Prometheus scraper'
        test: 'smoke-tests/gp-001/metrics-reachable.test'
        expected: pass
```

#### Example 3: Inherited Verification Contract — FedRAMP Moderate REST Microservice (GP-007)

GP-007 extends GP-001 with FedRAMP-specific controls. The contract declares inheritance to avoid re-specifying all 14 GP-001 checks:

```yaml
verification_contract:
  path_id: 'GP-007'
  path_name: 'FedRAMP Moderate REST Microservice on AKS'
  version: '1.0.0'
  inherits_from:
    path_id: 'GP-001'
    version: '1.2.0'
    # All 14 GP-001 checks are inherited — do not re-specify them.
    # Override only if GP-007 tightens a GP-001 requirement.

  # FedRAMP-specific additions only:
  conformance_checks:
    additional_checks:
      - id: 'FED-001'
        check_type: 'policy-as-code'
        layer: 3
        description: 'FIPS 140-2 validated cryptography module declared'
        rule: 'crypto.module_name matches /fips/ or provider == "openssl-fips"'
        required: true
      - id: 'FED-002'
        check_type: 'fitness-function'
        layer: 2
        description: 'Session timeout <= 30 minutes enforced'
        test_reference: 'tests/fedramp/session-timeout.test'
        required: true
      - id: 'FED-003'
        check_type: 'fitness-function'
        layer: 2
        description: 'MFA requirement annotation present on all auth endpoints'
        test_reference: 'tests/fedramp/mfa-annotation.test'
        required: true
      - id: 'FED-004'
        check_type: 'conformance'
        layer: 1
        description: 'FedRAMP impact level label present on K8s namespace'
        rule: 'labels["fedramp-impact-level"] in ["low", "moderate", "high"]'
        required: true
      - id: 'FED-005'
        check_type: 'policy-as-code'
        layer: 3
        description: 'No non-FedRAMP-authorized cloud service endpoints in egress'
        policy: 'policies/fedramp/authorized-endpoints.rego'
        required: true
      - id: 'FED-006'
        check_type: 'runtime'
        layer: 4
        description: 'Audit log shipped to FedRAMP boundary SIEM within 5 minutes'
        monitor: 'monitors/fedramp/audit-log-latency.yaml'
        required: true

  inherited_override:
    # GP-001 allows 'warn' for INF-001 during migration. GP-007 requires 'deny'.
    - id: 'INF-001'
      override: 'expected: deny'
      rationale: 'FedRAMP Moderate requires encryption at rest with no warn-period tolerance'
```

**Developer usage:** A service team adopting GP-007 runs the standard verification pipeline. The framework resolves the `inherits_from` reference, loads all 14 GP-001 checks plus the 6 FedRAMP additions, and executes 20 total checks. The team sees a single consolidated report — no separate GP-001 and GP-007 reports.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- Author the Verification Contract at the same time as the Golden Path definition, in the same PR. Never treat the contract as a follow-on deliverable.
- Cover all eight verification types. If a type genuinely does not apply to a path (e.g., a static site has no database connectivity to check), document the explicit exemption with the rationale.
- Validate the contract by running it against a known-good path implementation before ARB submission. A contract that has never been executed may contain incorrect check references.
page_texts.31:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- **Aspirational contract items**: Referencing a check that does not yet exist in the verification infrastructure. All checks in a contract must be executable before the path is published.
- **Contract drift**: Updating the Golden Path without updating the Verification Contract. Version-lock the contract to the path version to prevent this.
- **Overlapping checks across layers**: The same rule enforced at both Layer 1 and Layer 2. This is not a problem per se but increases maintenance overhead — prefer the earliest layer that can detect the violation.

### Compliance Requirements

The Verification Contract is the mechanism by which HIPAA and FedRAMP compliance claims on Golden Paths become auditable. The contract maps each compliance-relevant structural rule to an automated check, and the Compliance Evidence Store (PTN-GOV-AI-004) stores the timestamped results of every check. Together, they constitute a continuous compliance evidence chain.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#real-world-example-1]

### Real-World Example 1

**Context:** ARB is reviewing the GP-001 (HIPAA REST Microservice) proposal.
**Implementation:** Platform Engineering submits the path definition and the complete Verification Contract simultaneously. The ARB reviews both. An ARB member notices the contract has no check for "PHI audit events emitted on all data access operations" — a key HIPAA requirement. They reject the path pending addition of this check. Platform Engineering adds the fitness function check and resubmits. The contract now covers 8/8 types.
**Outcome:** The ARB review process caught a genuine compliance gap before the path was published and adopted by AI agents.
page_texts.39:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#real-world-example-2]

### Real-World Example 2

**Context:** A product team reports that their service, built from GP-001, is passing all conformance gates but generating PHI in logs in a specific edge case.
**Implementation:** The Platform Engineering team adds a new fitness function check to the contract: a pattern-matching test that scans log output samples for PHI field patterns. GP-001 is patched (PATCH version bump). All adopters run the new check and the edge case is caught for all services simultaneously.
**Outcome:** One contract update improves the compliance posture of every service built from GP-001 — demonstrating the leverage of catalog-level verification.
page_texts.40:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#real-world-example-3]

### Real-World Example 3

**Context:** Platform Engineering is authoring GP-007 (FedRAMP Moderate REST Microservice on AKS), which extends GP-001 (HIPAA REST Microservice). GP-007 adds FedRAMP-specific controls (FIPS-validated cryptography, session timeout enforcement, multi-factor authentication check) on top of all GP-001 controls.

**Implementation:** Rather than re-specifying all 14 GP-001 checks in the GP-007 Verification Contract, the team uses contract inheritance. The GP-007 contract declares `inherits_from: GP-001-v1.2.0` and adds 6 new FedRAMP-specific checks. When the pipeline evaluates a GP-007 service, it executes all 14 inherited GP-001 checks plus the 6 GP-007 additions — 20 checks total. When GP-001 is updated to v1.3.0 (adding a new check), GP-007 inherits the update automatically at its next minor version bump.

**Outcome:** The FedRAMP path is authored with 30% less Verification Contract content than a standalone authoring approach. Updates to the base HIPAA path propagate correctly to FedRAMP without manual re-specification. The ARB approves both the path and the inheritance model as a reusable contract authorship pattern.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#scenario-1-ai-agent-output-validation]

#### Scenario 1: AI Agent Output Validation

An autonomous AI agent generates a new service from GP-001. The CI/CD pipeline executes the full Verification Contract. Three checks fail: the OpenAPI spec is missing the health endpoint definition, the Prometheus metrics endpoint is not configured, and the HIPAA compliance annotation is absent. The pipeline blocks. The agent is fed the failing check output as context and regenerates the relevant sections. On rebuild, all checks pass.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#scenario-2-compliance-audit-response]

#### Scenario 2: Compliance Audit Response

An auditor asks: "Can you demonstrate that your HIPAA-scoped services enforce encryption at rest?" The response: query the Compliance Evidence Store for all services declaring GP-001 and return the evidence records for check `INF-001` (encryption at rest) over the audit period. The auditor receives timestamped, automated evidence for 100% of covered services with no manual assembly.
page_texts.44:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#scenario-3-contract-version-migration]

#### Scenario 3: Contract Version Migration

GP-001 is bumped to v1.3.0 with a new required check: `OBS-003` — trace context must be injected in all outbound HTTP calls. The Verification Contract is updated to v1.3.0 concurrent with the path update. All 18 services built on GP-001 v1.2.0 receive an automated notification: "Your service is pinned to GP-001 v1.2.0. Version 1.3.0 introduces 1 new required check (OBS-003). To migrate: update your `context.yaml` to v1.3.0 and verify the fitness function suite passes on next pipeline run." Twelve services migrate within 2 sprints. Six services open exception requests for the trace injection requirement (they use a service mesh that handles it transparently). Platform Engineering evaluates and adds a contract exemption for service-mesh-managed trace injection, closing all 6 exceptions.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#before-problem-state]

#### Before (Problem State)

- **Conformance claim**: "This service was built from the HIPAA Golden Path" — stated in a developer README; unverifiable and unverified
- **Auditor question**: "How do you know it still conforms after 6 months of changes?" — answered with "we reviewed it at code review"
- **Evidence**: PR comments in GitHub from the original authoring review — not structured, not timestamped to each build, not covering all compliance properties
- **AI output trustworthiness**: No framework to determine whether AI-generated output is architecturally sound; human review is the only gate
- **Compliance gap detection**: A new path requirement (e.g., updated secret management standard) has no mechanism to propagate to existing implementations
page_texts.47:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#after-solution-state]

#### After (Solution State)

- **Conformance claim**: "This service is built from GP-001 v1.2.0. Here are 14 automated check results from the latest build, all passing, timestamped, covering encryption at rest (INF-001), PHI in logs (OBS-002), external secrets integration (SEC-002), and all other Verification Contract checks"
- **Auditor question**: Answered with a query against the Compliance Evidence Store returning all 14 check results for every build over the audit period
- **Evidence**: Structured JSON records in the evidence store, generated at every pipeline run, indexed by check ID, service, and build timestamp
- **AI output trustworthiness**: AI-generated services are held to the same Verification Contract as human-authored services; conformance is provable for both
- **Compliance gap detection**: A new check in the Verification Contract propagates to all adopters via the path version notification system on next pipeline run

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-003-verification-contract-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem:** A Golden Path without a machine-executable verification specification is a recommendation, not an enforceable standard — compliance claims are assertions with no automated evidence.

**Solution:** A Verification Contract is the mandatory YAML specification accompanying every Golden Path, mapping each structural rule to an automated check across four verification layers. A path without a complete contract cannot be published.

**When to Use:**
- During authorship of every Golden Path (concurrent, not after)
- When updating a path with new rules
- When evaluating AI-generated output conformance

**Key Benefits:**
- Conformance is provable, not asserted
- Compliance evidence is generated automatically at every build
- AI-generated and human-authored output are held to the same standard

**Implementation Complexity:** Medium

**Prerequisites:** All four verification layers operational (PTN-INFRA-GOV-001, PTN-APP-GOV-001, PTN-INFRA-GOV-002, PTN-APP-GOV-003), Compliance Evidence Store active (PTN-GOV-AI-004).

**Related Patterns:** PTN-GOV-AI-001, PTN-GOV-AI-004, PTN-GOV-AI-006, PTN-INFRA-GOV-001, PTN-APP-GOV-001, PTN-INFRA-GOV-002, PTN-APP-GOV-003
